label: Chong Bok
sub: Flashpoint clash site, May 28 2025 -- one Cambodian soldier killed near this undemarcated border point.

label: Hill 745 (Phu Makhuea)
sub: Disputed high ground in Nam Yuen district where Cambodian entrenchment was reported May 17, 2025.

label: Chong An Ma Crossing
sub: Site of the July 23, 2025 landmine blast that injured five Thai soldiers and triggered the outbreak of open fighting.

label: Prasat Ta Muen Thom
sub: 11th-century temple complex where fighting broke out July 24, 2025; remains one of the most contested sectors of the frontier.

label: Preah Vihear Temple
sub: Awarded to Cambodia by the ICJ in 1962; the surrounding land border remains undemarcated and periodically contested.

label: Prasat Ta Krabei
sub: Contested temple site near Ta Muen Thom; scene of artillery exchanges during the 2008-2011 clashes and renewed tension in 2025.

label: O'Smach
sub: Cambodian border town in Oddar Meanchey province; evacuation point for thousands fleeing cross-border shelling.

label: Chong Chom-O'Smach Crossing
sub: Key crossing point between Surin province and Oddar Meanchey; repeatedly closed amid clashes and ceasefire violations.

label: Surin-Sisaket Displacement Corridor
sub: Thai border provinces hosting the bulk of Thailand's IDP shelters during both the July and December 2025 escalations.

label: Sisaket Border Sector
sub: Site of a February 24, 2026 exchange of fire after Cambodian forces fired a 40mm grenade round near a Thai patrol.

label: Poipet-Aranyaprathet Crossing
sub: Major commercial border crossing repeatedly shut during escalations, disrupting billions of dollars in bilateral trade.

label: Ban Pak Kard Crossing, Chanthaburi
sub: Site of the December 27, 2025 signing of the second ceasefire agreement between Thai and Cambodian defense ministers.

label: Trat Province
sub: Thai coastal border province whose tourism economy absorbed heavy losses (over 1 billion baht in nine days) during the December 2025 fighting.

label: Chong Kal Displacement Camp
sub: Major Cambodian IDP camp in Oddar Meanchey province, part of the government's emergency evacuation response.

label: Banteay Meanchey IDP Sites
sub: Province hosting some of the largest concentrations of displaced Cambodians, including roughly 2,000 people in shelters as of late December 2025.

label: Battambang Shelter Sites
sub: One of four Cambodian provinces hosting pagoda, market and camp-based shelters for civilians fleeing border fighting.

label: Siem Reap Province IDP Areas
sub: Among the provinces with the highest recorded displacement figures as of January 1, 2026, per World Vision reporting.

label: Preah Vihear Province Shelters
sub: Housed roughly 600 displaced families as of late December 2025, near the epicenter of temple-area fighting.

label: Aranyaprathet Fence Sector
sub: Approved site for a planned 10km permanent border fence with triple-layer barbed wire and CCTV in a disputed sector.

label: Chanthaburi Pilot Fence (BM 52-54)
sub: First 1.3km segment of reinforced-concrete border fencing completed by Thailand in April 2026, between border markers 52 and 54.

label: Sa Kaeo Border Sector
sub: Thai province along a heavily militarized stretch of frontier that saw repeated clashes during both 2025 escalations.

label: Ubon Ratchathani Province
sub: Thai province containing the Chong Bok and Chong An Ma flashpoints where the conflict's first clashes occurred.

label: Chong Sa-ngam
sub: Border pass in Sisaket province that saw renewed fighting during the December 2025 collapse of the first ceasefire.

label: Oddar Meanchey Province
sub: Cambodian province bordering Surin and Sisaket; among the earliest areas to see civilian evacuations in May-July 2025.

label: Emerald Triangle Tripoint
sub: Where the Thai, Cambodian and Laotian borders meet near Chong Bok -- a historically ambiguous frontier zone at the heart of the dispute.

label: Ta Kwai Temple / Hill 350
sub: Khmer sanctuary and adjacent high ground roughly 12km east of Ta Muen Thom; JIC inspection on Aug 20, 2026 reported Cambodian tank and troop buildup nearby.

label: Thma Da, Pursat Province
sub: Site of a disputed Chinese-owned hotel where the owner alleged Thai troops occupied and looted property; Thailand denies the claim as of Aug 19, 2026.

label: Ban Nong Chan, Khok Sung District
sub: Sa Kaeo border village opposite reinforced Cambodian positions; JIC raised vigilance here on Aug 22, 2026 and it is also the subject of UN-rapporteur civilian-return calls Thailand disputes.

label: Hill 500 / An Seh (Chong An Ma)
sub: Contested area at the Chong An Ma crossing that Thailand designates Hill 500 and administers under the Dec 27, 2025 Joint Statement; Cambodia calls it An Seh, within Choam Ksan district of Preah Vihear province, and protested PM Anutin's Aug 23, 2026 troop visit as a sovereignty violation.
